sources.entry: Interview: Discussing agents' tracing, observability, and debugging with Ismail Pelaseyed, the founder of Superagent

summary.name: Superagent
summary.one_liner: Superagent is an open-source platform for building AI agents aimed at no-code and web developers, with a free cloud version, and this E2B interview covers its founder's views on agent tracing, observability, and debugging.
use_cases: building no-code AI agents for apps
tracing and monitoring LLM agent steps
summary.what_it_does: The page is an interview with Ismail Pelaseyed, founder of Superagent, about agent challenges. Superagent is described as a platform for web and no-code developers, with two main agent types: retrieval chatbots for Q&A over documents, and action-based assistants run via chat or API. Its architecture stores agent configurations in a database and an API service creates and runs agents on the fly, using Langchain and LlamaIndex, with a move toward a queue-based system. The interview explains that debugging today relies on end users reporting problems in Discord, and that current tracing shows failures without explaining why they happened or how to fix them. The team has a run-viewing UI similar to LangSmith for stepping through agent runs.
notable: Completely open-source platform with a free cloud version
Wraps tested agent types so memory, vectorization and agent logic are handled automatically
Per-run UI for viewing each agent step, similar to LangSmith
Reported about 2000 users and 1500+ agents running daily in production after about two months
caveats: Agent architecture is described as early stage, making configuration for specific use cases hard
Tracing lacks root-cause explanations and suggested fixes, which the founder says are needed
Team is reworking infrastructure to move agents into a queue instead of running them on the fly
